redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_journal_writes.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1, but no test was collected or none reached an assertion: SELFTEST FAILED: 137/138 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD, PWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: Added a shared window helper in hooks/_config.py (writer_key, record_call_start, call_start, changed_in_window, ts_epoch, window_peers, window_note). journal-writes Pre now notes the call start for Bash/mcp (one small atomic write, no read; bench-hooks --gate exit 0). Post sweep: a moved path whose (target, stateHash) matches a non-hook row stamped inside the window gets no row; an unaccounted move with a peer evidenced in the window (other session's row inside it, or live lock) is journaled with sessionId None and 'changed during this command; this session or <peer> wrote it'; no peer -> attributed as before; no start -> old behaviour. guard-bash-writes: new paths whose mtime precedes the call start are absorbed; manifest paths under a live peer's lock that moved in-window get WINDOW_LOCK_TEMPLATE (both candidates, no stop) unless the command text names the write. Tests: wn1-wn3 (journal), wn1-wn4 (guard), cw1-cw4 (_config); so_pre in the existing so group moves its window past earlier rows (second-resolution stamps). Docs: SECURITY.md bullet, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md two paragraphs. Hot path adds: a write in Pre; reads of the start file only after a move/new dirty path; the trail read only after a move.  Not run: the --spaced and sweep were run as listed. Note: the unattributed marker is only used when a peer is evidenced; a lone writer stays attributed (otherwise every shell-made manifest write would lose its author).
outcome.descriptive: A peer's verb write or earlier file change is no longer journaled or alarmed as the current Bash call's own; ambiguous cases name both candidates and order no stop.

claims: claims: (1) hooks/_config.py window helpers are used by both hooks - evidence: grep call sites record_call_start/call_start/changed_in_window; (2) bench-hooks --gate exit 0, sweep exit 0, --spaced exit 0, ruff 0, vermin 0, check-git-pipeline 0; (3) the red proof is the helper's, not mine.
